study type: Cross-sectional analysis of a birth cohort baseline
exposure: nine years or less of schooling
lowest quartiles of the wealth index
cohort: The study participants were postpartum women (26.2% adolescents) from the MINA-Brazil birth cohort in Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, Brazil, comparing characteristics of adolescent and adult mothers.
finding: Poverty, low schooling, primigravidity, low pre-pregnancy BMI, urinary tract infection during pregnancy, and few prenatal consultations were associated with childbirth during adolescence in the studied Brazilian municipality.
cross-section timing: Baseline data analysis of postpartum women from the MINA-Brazil birth cohort.
